title.en: Not anything: two negatives working together

summary.en: Recognise the pattern before and after the verb.

body.en:
In the Boris taster, Arianna interrupts the new intern with *No, tu non vuoi niente*: ‘No, you do not want anything.’

The first *no* is a standalone refusal. Inside the following clause, *non* comes before *vuoi*, while *niente* comes after it. These two negatives work together in ordinary Italian. Translating them mechanically as ‘not nothing’ would give the wrong English meaning.

The word *vuoi* addresses one person familiarly. The speaker includes *tu* to make her correction forceful; the verb ending already identifies the person.

Replay the original line and distinguish the standalone refusal from the negative pattern inside the sentence.
